text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: metrics-pipeline-prod - alert=PrometheusScrapeFailures count>10 for job=exporters/node_exporter
incident-bot: Alert details: failing_targets=[10.4.22.11:9100,10.4.22.12:9100], error=HTTP_500, recent_failures=15 in 5m
Sam: acked — I'm oncall for eng-sre right now, taking lead. pinging oncall runbook.
Alex: oncall runbook opened. first check: are the exporters actually up? Jordan can you confirm if target VMs are healthy?
Jordan: looking at host health — both nodes show high load and memory pressure, node_exporter logs show repeated scrape handler OOM. Grafana: scrape_success rate dropped from 0.98 -> 0.4 at 2314509600. Prometheus queue shows scrape backlog ~1200 samples.
Maya: customer impact? any customers reporting alerts?
Jordan: CAT dashboard shows a handful of customers with missing infra metrics; no active support tickets yet, but internal alerting for downstream analytics is firing. Likely impact to cost dashboards and onboarding demos.
Lee: possible quick mitigation: remove the offending targets from scrape pool while we stabilize. Or scale exporter replica set if it's a k8s-hosted exporter.
Sam: these are node_exporters on bare-metal; can't just scale. Let's (1) temporarily reduce scrape frequency for that scrape_job to 60s -> 300s, (2) mark targets as maintenance in PD/ops, (3) try to restart node_exporter on the two hosts.
Alex: agreed. I can edit prometheus config via the CDN config manager. Applying a flood-safe change: set scrape_interval for job=exporters/node_exporter to 300s and target_timeout to 10s.
Alex: applying change now. copying snippet:
```
- job_name: exporters/node_exporter
  scrape_interval: 300s
  scrape_timeout: 10s
  static_configs:
    - targets: ["10.4.22.11:9100","10.4.22.12:9100"]
```
incident-bot: Config change detected and reload started (prometheus-reload-operator).
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: if alert unacked for 8m escalate to pager duty escalation policy level 2.
Sam: restarting node_exporter on 10.4.22.11 via ssh.
Sam: ran: `sudo systemctl restart node-exporter` — logs show restart succeeded but memory still creeps. pulling /var/log/node_exporter.log snippet:
```
panic: runtime: out of memory
goroutine 1 [running]:
main.main() ... node_exporter v1.2.2
```
Lee: that's consistent with binary leak on that version. we should patch to v1.3.0, but patching prod hosts is heavy. Short-term: disable the collector that's leaking (filesystem collector) on those hosts.
Jordan: I can update node_exporter flags via salt for just those two hosts: `--collector.filesystem.ignored-mount-points` or disable entire collector with `--no-collector.filesystem`.
Maya: good plan. Sam, can you temporarily disable filesystem collector on 10.4.22.11 & .12?
Sam: doing it now. running: `sudo systemctl stop node-exporter && node_exporter --no-collector.filesystem &` (wrapped to keep process).
Sam: restarted with no filesystem collector, memory usage stabilized on 11. CPU load still high but no OOM. scrape_success on prometheus started increasing within 30s.
Jordan: confirmed: scrape_success for those targets back to 0.95, backlog draining. kafka consumer lag for metrics-ingest reduced from 14k -> 3k in last 6m.
Maya: nice. What about longer-term? we should schedule patching and maybe add oom-killer policy.
Alex: created a ticket: INF-4821 "node_exporter v1.2.2 OOM on busy hosts — patch to v1.3.0 and hardening". assigning to eng-platform.
Sam: PD note: acknowledged -> resolved suppressed? we should close the pager once backlog < 500 and scrape_success > 0.9 for 10m.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert acknowledged by Sam at 2314509900. escalation paused.
Lee: also rebalanced a couple Kafka partitions to speed up consumer recovery; used `kafka-reassign-partitions` with dry-run then execute.
Lee: command used:
```
kubectl -n infra exec -it kafka-0 -- kafka-reassign-partitions --zookeeper zk:2181 --reassignment-json-file reassign.json --execute
```
Jordan: monitoring shows consumer group metrics-ingest lag trending down. no messages dropped.
Maya: customer impact update: we saw partial missing infra metrics in dashboards for ~18 minutes for ~6 customers. engineering impact low, product dashboards affected but no billing issues. ops to notify infra-oncall and CS.
Sam: status update to ops and CS posted in #customer-impact with summary and timeframe.
Alex: preparing handoff: my shift ends in 20m. Maya, can you take follow-up until 10:30 PDT? I'll leave commands and notes in the incident ticket.
Maya: taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring until backlog < 100 and scrape_success stable.
incident-bot: Escalation timer cleared at 2314511400 — no further escalation.
Sam: confirming final checks — backlog at 230 samples, scrape_success 0.993 for last 5m, exporters stable.
Maya: closing PD incident and marking incident doc. Root cause: node_exporter v1.2.2 memory leak on filesystem collector under heavy IO; mitigated by disabling collector and rebalancing consumers; full fix scheduled (INF-4821).
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert resolved at 2314513000 by Maya. :white_check_mark:
